noah: heads-up - onboarding sampleapp (node) shows embed helper parity bug. When a batch retry happens mid-flight, returned embeddings misalign (null slot + duplicate). gist with repro in the issue.
rachel: can you paste request/response? is it missing items or shuffled? :confused:
noah: sent 3 inputs via helper; got back [e1, null, e2] where e2 corresponds to input 3. Looks like index mapping drifted after a retry.
omar: node batcher uses positional mapping (map by queue index at promise resolution). if a retry re-enqueues part of the batch the index offsets are wrong. python/go clients reconcile by per-item token id. parity gap.
noah: logs show original chunk-id c-1 then retry c-2; client merged responses by offsets.
qa-bot: suggested mitigation: set EMBED_BATCH=1 for quickstart and disable client retry until fix applied.
rachel: proposed fix: inject item_id into each request input and echo it in response so client maps deterministically. also add stableOrder flag in node helper for opt-in UID mapping.
omar: I'll open PR: map-by-itemid, add stableOrder=false default for compatibility, update onboarding sampleapp to recommend stableOrder=true. adding unit + flaky e2e simulating intermittent 401 mid-batch.
noah: also noticed envelope inconsistencies across runtimes: some responses used data[i].embeddings vs data[i].embedding. sampleapps should accept both for now; server should standardize to singular in docs.
qa-bot: ci: redwood-node PR queued (job 9012).
rachel: filed GH issue redwood/node#1345 with repro and logs and linked here. added temporary onboarding note: "If embeddings look off, set EMBED_BATCH=1 and disable client retries."
noah: thanks — catching this during onboarding prevents bad first impressions. :thumbsup:
